name: input.move
description: Move the mouse cursor without clicking. Absolute coordinates by default; pass `relative: true` to add `x` and `y` as deltas from the current position.

x.description: Target X (absolute, virtual-screen) or X delta (relative). Off-screen results are clamped; the clamped value is reported back as `actual_position`.

relative.description: Treat `x` and `y` as deltas added to the current cursor position. Default false (absolute coordinates).

x.description: Actual X the cursor landed at after any clamping.

y.description: Actual Y the cursor landed at.

x-implementations.name: send_input
x-implementations.description: Win32 `GetCursorPos` (when `relative: true`) + `SendInput(MOUSEEVENTF_MOVE | MOUSEEVENTF_ABSOLUTE)`. The MOUSEEVENTF_ABSOLUTE form takes 0..65535 normalised coords mapped to the primary monitor; agent maps from virtual-screen pixels to MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK + MOUSEEVENTF_ABSOLUTE for multi-monitor reach.

x-implementations.name: set_cursor_pos
x-implementations.description: Win32 `SetCursorPos` legacy fallback. Bypasses the input-event queue, so apps that hook mouse events via SetWindowsHookEx don't see the move. Used only when SendInput fails (rare).

windows-modern.description: SendInput with MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK | MOUSEEVENTF_ABSOLUTE for multi-monitor virtual-screen reach. UIPI silently drops moves directed at higher-IL windows; agent can't detect this for moves (unlike clicks) so callers should verify post-move position when targeting elevated apps.

windows-classic.description: SendInput on NT 5+ (with MOUSEEVENTF_VIRTUALDESK on NT 5.1+ for multi-monitor); SetCursorPos on NT 4 / 9x. NT 4 single-monitor only — multi-monitor coords clamp to the primary monitor.
